title: Pandas Data Cleaning Basics: Nulls and Duplicates
audience: Complete beginners to data engineering who know basic Python (variables, functions, lists, for loops) but have little or no prior experience with pandas.
prerequisites: Basic Python (variables, functions, for loops, running a .py script).
Comfort opening and reading a CSV file in a text editor or spreadsheet.
No prior pandas or data engineering experience required.
outcomes: Explain why missing values and duplicate rows silently break downstream analysis.
Detect missing values in a pandas DataFrame with isna()/isnull() and summarize them per column.
Decide, per column, whether to drop or fill a missing value, and apply that decision with dropna() and fillna().
Detect exact and key-based duplicate rows with duplicated() and understand the keep parameter.
Remove duplicate rows deterministically with drop_duplicates(), choosing which occurrence to keep.
Combine null-handling and deduplication into one small, readable, testable cleaning script.
Validate a cleaning script's output against expected row counts and values with pytest.
business_scenario: GreenLeaf Analytics runs a customer feedback form for a small retail chain. The raw daily export, customer_feedback_raw.csv, comes straight from the form backend and is messy: some customers left the rating field blank, some entries are missing the email address needed to identify the customer, some optional fields (comments, region) are blank, and a number of customers accidentally submitted the form twice for the same date (sometimes an exact repeat, sometimes a corrected second answer). Before the weekly satisfaction report can be trusted, this raw export must be cleaned: rows missing required fields must be removed, optional blanks must be filled with a clear placeholder instead of staying null, and duplicate submissions for the same customer and date must be collapsed down to a single, most-recent row.
deliverable: A Python script (clean_customer_feedback.py) that reads student-lab/datasets/customer_feedback_raw.csv, drops rows missing a required field (customer_email or rating), fills optional blanks (comments, region) with clear placeholder text, deduplicates repeat submissions per (customer_email, survey_date) by keeping the last occurrence, and writes the result to output/clean_feedback.csv, verified by an automated pytest suite.
validation_criteria: pytest against tests/test_clean_customer_feedback.py exits with status 0.
Rows with a missing customer_email or a missing rating are absent from clean_feedback.csv.
clean_feedback.csv has no null/NaN values in any column.
For every (customer_email, survey_date) pair that appeared more than once in the raw file, only the last occurrence (by submission_id order) survives in clean_feedback.csv.
acquired_skills: Inspecting a DataFrame for missing values with isna()/isnull() and .sum().
Choosing between dropna() and fillna() per column based on whether a field is required or optional.
Detecting duplicate rows with duplicated() and understanding first/last/False keep semantics.
Removing duplicate rows deterministically with drop_duplicates(subset=..., keep=...).
Structuring a small, readable pandas cleaning script as testable functions instead of one long block.
Writing pytest tests that assert on DataFrame shape, null counts, and specific row survival.
